prompt: Inside a click handler, `setMonday('2026-10-26')` runs and the next line logs `monday`. What does it print?
hint: `monday` is this render's constant.

choices.text: `2026-10-26`, the value just set
choices.why: The setter schedules the next render; it does not change the constant you hold.

choices.text: `undefined`, because state is being updated at that moment
choices.why: The variable keeps its value for the whole render; there is no in-between.

choices.text: The old value
choices.why: Right. The new value arrives in the next render.

choices.text: An error saying state was read after it was set
choices.why: Reading it is allowed; it is simply the snapshot.

prompt: `TwoWeeks` called `setMonday(addDays(monday, 7))` twice. Why did the week move by one?
hint: What did each call compute its value from?

choices.text: React ignores a second setter call in one event
choices.why: Both calls were applied; they asked for the same value.

choices.text: Strict mode undid one of them
choices.why: Strict mode does not undo setter calls.

choices.text: Both computed the 26th from the same snapshot
choices.why: Right. Asking twice for the 26th is asking once.

choices.text: `addDays` returned the same day twice because of time zones
choices.why: `addDays` worked; it was given the same input twice.

prompt: A handler calls three different setters. How many times does the component render because of that click?
hint: The section names the behaviour.

choices.text: Once, after all three are applied
choices.why: Right. That is batching.

choices.text: Three, one per setter
choices.why: Calls in one event are collected and applied together.

choices.text: None until the next click
choices.why: It renders right after the event.

choices.text: Twice, because strict mode is on
choices.why: Strict mode doubles the call, not the number of renders the event causes.

prompt: Why does the planner write `useState(() => mondayOf(today()))` and not `useState(mondayOf(today()))`?
hint: When is the initial value used?

choices.text: The second form is a type error
choices.why: Both compile; they differ in when the date is computed.

choices.text: So the week updates at midnight
choices.why: Neither form updates by itself.

choices.text: Functions are faster than strings
choices.why: The value is a string either way.

choices.text: So the date is worked out once
choices.why: Right. React calls the function once.

prompt: With two updater functions, which day of November did the week reach after one click?
hint: Two weeks after Monday 19 October.

prompt: With the updater form, the log after both calls still said `2026-10-19`. Why?
hint: Who saw the intermediate value?

choices.text: The updater functions had not run yet
choices.why: Whether or not they had, `monday` is this render's constant and never changes.

choices.text: The updater form does not work inside handlers
choices.why: It worked: the week moved two weeks.

choices.text: The log is printed before the click
choices.why: It is printed inside the handler, after both calls.

choices.text: `monday` is the snapshot; the queue saw the new values
choices.why: Right. The 26th existed only between the two functions.

prompt: A counter's button runs `setCount(count + 1)` and a timer that fired in the same moment runs `setCount(count + 1)` too, both from the same render. What fixes it so both count?
hint: The new value depends on the old one.

choices.text: Calling `setCount(count + 2)` in the button and nothing in the timer
choices.why: That counts two whenever the button is pressed, timer or not.

choices.text: Storing `count` in a variable outside the component
choices.why: React would not render when it changed.

choices.text: `setCount((c) => c + 1)` in both
choices.why: Right. Each function receives what the last returned.

choices.text: Turning strict mode off
choices.why: Strict mode is not involved.

prompt: After "Next week", the broken `WeekSummary` showed "Week of 26 Oct 2026" and "80 of 195". Why the old totals?
hint: When is an initial value used?

choices.text: The totals were copied into state once and never recomputed
choices.why: Right. An initial value is used on the first render only.

choices.text: The new sessions had not loaded yet
choices.why: Nothing loads; the sessions were in the props.

choices.text: `minutes` caches its results
choices.why: `minutes` is a plain sum, computed every time it is called.

choices.text: React skipped rendering `WeekSummary`
choices.why: It rendered: the week line changed.

prompt: Sort each value of the planner: stored as state, or computed while rendering.
hint: Ask what would set it.

prompt: A screen shows a search box and the courses whose names match it. Which should be state?
hint: One of them the user sets; the other follows from it.

choices.text: The matching courses, so they are ready when the screen renders
choices.why: They follow from the text and the courses, and a copy would go stale.

choices.text: Both, kept in step with an extra function
choices.why: That is the copy the section warns against, with the job of keeping it in step.

choices.text: Neither: read the box's value from the DOM
choices.why: React would not render when the text changed.

choices.text: The text typed
choices.why: Right. The list is a filter computed from it each render.

prompt: Why do `openId` and `sessions` live in `App`?
hint: Who reads them?

choices.text: A component's state has to be declared in the root of the app
choices.why: Any component can hold state; `Probe` did in lesson 3.

choices.text: `CourseScreen` cannot have state
choices.why: It can; it would just hide it from the first screen.

choices.text: Both screens read them, and `App` is above both
choices.why: Right. State goes in the closest common parent of its readers.

choices.text: `App` renders less often than its children
choices.why: Placement is about who reads the state, not render counts.

prompt: Moving state to the closest shared parent of the components that read it is called lifting state ___.
hint: A direction.

prompt: Why does `openId` need its type written, `useState<string | null>(null)`?
hint: What would TypeScript infer from `null` alone?

choices.text: From `null` it would infer a type that cannot later hold an id
choices.why: Right. The annotation says it holds a string or nothing.

choices.text: Because `null` is not allowed in state
choices.why: It is allowed, and here it means no course is open.

choices.text: Because Vite requires generic arguments
choices.why: Vite removes types and never reads them.

choices.text: To make the second screen render first
choices.why: Types do not affect rendering order.

prompt: After ticking the Statistics session of 21 October, how many minutes did the summary say were done?
hint: 80 before, plus the session just done.

prompt: `CourseScreen` writes `[...sessions].sort(…)`. What goes wrong with `sessions.sort(…)`?
hint: Who owns the array?

choices.text: `sort` returns `undefined`
choices.why: It returns the sorted array; the trouble is that it is the same array.

choices.text: It sorts `App`'s state in place, from inside a child
choices.why: Right. A child would be changing data it was given.

choices.text: Strings cannot be compared with `localeCompare`
choices.why: They can, and these sort correctly.

choices.text: Nothing: both are the same
choices.why: One sorts a copy, the other sorts the original.

prompt: How does React decide that new state differs from old?
hint: For objects, one question.

choices.text: It compares every field, recursively
choices.why: It never looks inside; that is why mutation hides.

choices.text: It serialises both to JSON and compares the strings
choices.why: Far too slow, and not what it does.

choices.text: It asks the browser whether the page changed
choices.why: The page is the result of the comparison, not the input.

choices.text: `Object.is` on the two values
choices.why: Right. For an object: is it the same object?

prompt: Without strict mode, put what happened after the mutating `toggleDone` in order.
hint: The data changed before anything showed it.
items: `session.done` becomes true inside the same array
React sees the same array and skips the render

prompt: Under strict mode, the mutating `toggleDone` left the total at 80. Why?
hint: How many times does strict mode run an updater?

choices.text: It ran the updater twice, and it flipped `done` back
choices.why: Right. A pure updater gives the same answer twice; this one undid itself.

choices.text: Strict mode refuses state that mutates
choices.why: It refuses nothing; it repeated the function.

choices.text: The click did not reach the checkbox
choices.why: It reached it; without strict mode the total became 120.

choices.text: 80 was cached by `WeekSummary`
choices.why: `WeekSummary` computes its totals every render.

prompt: Match each change to the way that gives React a new array.
hint: The table at the end of the section.

prompt: In `all.map((s) => (s.id === id ? { ...s, done: !s.done } : s))`, which session objects are new?
hint: Look at what the function returns for the others.

choices.text: Every one of them
choices.why: The others are returned as they were, the same objects.

choices.text: None of them: `map` reuses the array
choices.why: `map` returns a new array, and the matching session is a new object.

choices.text: The one whose id matches
choices.why: Right. Five are reused and one is copied with a field replaced.

choices.text: The sessions of the open course
choices.why: Only the toggled one.

prompt: Which of these lines are safe updates of `sessions` state? Choose every one.
hint: Safe means a new array, and the old one untouched.

choices.text: `setSessions((all) => [...all, s])`
choices.why: Safe.

choices.text: `setSessions((all) => { all.push(s); return all })`
choices.why: Unsafe: same array, changed in place.

choices.text: `setSessions((all) => all.filter((x) => !x.done))`
choices.why: Safe.

choices.text: `setSessions((all) => all.toSorted(byDate))`
choices.why: Safe: `toSorted` returns a new array.

prompt: Ticking a session on the second screen changed the totals on the first. What made the first screen update?
hint: Nobody told `WeekSummary` anything.

choices.text: `CourseScreen` called `WeekSummary` directly
choices.why: Components do not call each other.

choices.text: `WeekSummary` stores the totals and `toggleDone` updates them too
choices.why: The totals are not stored anywhere.

choices.text: Its totals are computed from `sessions` on every render
choices.why: Right. New state, new render, new sums.

choices.text: The page reloaded on "Back to courses"
choices.why: Nothing reloaded; `openId` became `null`.
